items.message:
Higher than normal tides tomorrow morning may lead to flooding. 
Flooding is possible from 03:14AM to 07:14AM on 17/11/26. 
The highest tide level is expected to be at Christchurch Harbour and tidal stretches of the Lower Stour and Avon at 05:14AM on 17/11/2026 with a level of 1.24 mAODN and a South Westerly force 7 wind. Our threshold for issuing the Flood Alert for Christchurch Harbour is 1.20 mAODN so we anticipate only a small rise above this level. 
We are closely monitoring the situation .Start acting on your flood plan if you have one. 
Avoid beaches and coastal promenades, which may be flooded. Avoid coastal roads and low lying roads near rivers, which may be flooded. 
This message will be updated by 12:00PM on Tuesday 17 November or as the situation changes.

High tides, strong winds and large waves tomorrow afternoon may lead to flooding. 
Flooding is possible from 10:00 to 15:30 on Tuesday 17th November. 
Locations most affected will be coastal roads and footpaths near the South pier and Lifeboat station. The risk of flooding should reduce once the tide has passed. 
We are closely monitoring the situation . 
Take care and avoid walking, cycling or driving through flood water. 
This message will be updated by 9:00AM on Tuesday 17 November or as the situation changes.

items.message:
High river levels overnight may lead to flooding.
Flooding is possible on Monday 16 November .
Forecast levels may cause flooding to low lying land and roads close to rivers from around 10:30pm.

We expect rivers to remain high throughout the night and into Tuesday morning, though no flooding to properties is currently forecast.
We are closely monitoring the situation 
Take care and avoid walking, cycling or driving through flood water.  
This message will be updated by 11:00AM on Tuesday 17 November or as the situation changes.

There is no longer a threat of flooding, though standing water and debris may still remain.
Further rainfall is forecast.  
We will continue to monitor the situation and will issue further alerts or warnings if necessary.  
Continue to take care on waterside roads and footpaths and don't put yourself in unnecessary danger.

items.message:
High water levels today may lead to flooding.
Flooding is possible between 11am to 3pm today, Monday 16 November.
We expect to see high water levels around Potter Heigham, Wroxham boat yards and Ferry Road in Horning. Levels can take several hours to peak. River levels will remain high over the next couple of days.
We are closely monitoring the situation .
Avoid coastal roads and low lying roads near rivers, which may be flooded.  
This message will be updated by 10:00AM on Tuesday 17 November or as the situation changes.
